title: Marker strokes are flat and darken where they cross, and the airbrush sprays softly and builds up
goal: The marker and the airbrush look like their real tools: a marker stroke is one flat translucent colour that gets darker only where separate strokes cross, with a round or chisel tip, and the airbrush is a soft even spray that builds up the longer you hold it over one spot.
notes:
Umbrella: a-brush-tool-paints-with-realistic-charcoal-chal (the user's ask, 2026-10-24). Design: docs/design/brushes.md, read it first; its decisions are settled unless this task's runner finds one cannot work, in which case they say so in the log and in the doc.

Design doc decision 4 table, rows Marker and Airbrush. Marker: render the stroke into its own coverage mask with max (not sum), then composite the stroke with multiply over earlier strokes. Airbrush dwell needs time in the samples (StrokeSample.ms) and dabs emitted while the pointer is still.
acceptance: A marker stroke has even colour along its length even where it doubles back on itself, and a second stroke crossing it is darker in the overlap
Tip switches the marker between round and chisel, and a chisel stroke changes width with direction
Airbrush is a fine soft spray; holding the pointer still builds colour up; Flow and Softness each visibly change it

A walk with no flags paints with both by pointer drag, with real window pictures in the audit; measured bars for flatness (colour variance along a marker stroke) and build-up (airbrush density after a dwell vs a pass) that the round tip fails

log.note: deps set by the umbrella's planning run: pressing-b-picks-a-brush-that-paints-freehand-st

Adversarial review before building: a first-time user picks Marker from the Medium dropdown and drags, which works with no new controls. A Photoshop or Procreate user expects a marker that does not build up within one stroke and darkens on a second pass, and an airbrush that keeps spraying while held (Photoshop's 'build-up'); the app cannot deliver the hold without samples arriving while the mouse is still, so the canvas now ticks samples in while the button is down. Tip, Flow and Softness have no control in the capsule yet: that is each-brush-shows-its-own-settings-in-the-tool-op, already filed and in the design doc's slice order, so not a new prerequisite.

Chose multiply over the earlier paint on the same layer, written as an adjusted source-over (a·C·(1−Da+D)), over a CALayer multiply filter on the overlay, because the formula makes the live overlay land exactly as drawn (walk: 0.05% apart on a crossing) where a filter would multiply over the screenshot too. Chose a fixed 45 degree chisel nib over one that follows the stroke because a real chisel keeps its angle in the hand; tilt turning it is the dynamics slice. Chose time-based dwell dabs (one per 25 ms held within a dab's spacing) over counting events, so a trembling hand still builds up and live equals landed. Tried jitter on the airbrush to break rings at a crisp stroke's ends: it made the stroke lumpy, so widened the crisp cone's fall-off instead.

Moved the round-tip baseline in the dry media, pencil, paint and sheet tests from .marker to .oil (oil still uses the round tip until its slice). Added drag 'pause'/'pauseAt' to the walk harness (parsed and tested in PlaytestScriptTests). Pictures looked at before closing: the stroke sheet (flat marker, darker crossings, chisel width by direction, airbrush soft spray, dwell spot, softness 0 vs 100), and the walk's 3-marker-crossed-sc and 5-airbrush-built-up-sc with close crops: marker flat and darker only at the crossing; airbrush a soft spray line with a built-up dot at the pause and at the end (the walk holds still 0.3 s there before letting go).

Left rough, not filed (each covered or below the bar): Tip/Flow/Softness controls and per-medium size are folded into each-brush-shows-its-own-settings-in-the-tool-op; tilt/pressure for the marker belongs to the design doc's dynamics slice; a small held airbrush saturating to a dot is how the medium behaves. No sweep requested: the change touches only brush code and one harness option, and committing it triggers the rotating check.

Marker and airbrush shipped in 83b94294. Marker: max coverage within a stroke (flat even when it doubles back), multiplied over earlier paint so a crossing stroke is darker in the overlap, live overlay matches landed (walk 0.05% apart); Round and Chisel tips (chisel width changes with direction, render test: across the nib over 2x along it); Flow sets the ink. Airbrush: fine soft spray (mist plus droplets), a dab every 25 ms held, so it builds up; Flow and Softness each change it (render tests). Bars, by the real rasterizer: flat share 0.99 vs round tip 0.82 (bar 0.9); held a second vs a pass 3.3x vs round tip 1.0x (bar 1.6). marker-and-airbrush-walk paints both by pointer drag with no flags, incl. a 1.2 s hold, real window pictures in queue/audits/2026-10-25-marker-airbrush.json. Tip, Flow and Softness have no controls yet: that is each-brush-shows-its-own-settings-in-the-tool-op (noted there); the sheet shows them. Scripts/test.sh green (14,481 tests); brush, pencil and toolbar walks green.
